info.title: Giftly mobile and non-admin API
info.description: Generated from implemented backend routes for mobile integration. Admin routes are excluded. Screen and flow details are vendor extensions; unsupported screen features are future API work and have no route in this specification. Production payment routes currently return PAYMENTS_DISABLED until a verified Dhamen integration is available.

get.description: Call this only for process liveness, such as a load balancer or local diagnostics. It returns a static marker without checking PostgreSQL or Redis, so a successful response does not mean account screens can load. Mobile screens should not poll it as their data source. Use readiness separately when an operator needs to know whether backing services are available.
get.x-audience: Signed-out or signed-in; no bearer token

get.description: Use this for deployment readiness checks rather than a customer-facing screen. The handler probes both PostgreSQL and Redis and returns a dependency status map, with HTTP 503 when either is down. A phone app should surface normal request failures through its usual error states instead of polling this endpoint. Do not confuse readiness with the static liveness route.
get.x-audience: Signed-out or signed-in; no bearer token

get.description: Fetch active cities to populate registration, profile, and delivery selectors. Submit the selected id as a UUID relationship for courier registration, profile editing, or order creation. Display name_ar in Arabic and name in English. Existing name-based request fields remain for older clients, but send only one city field per request. Refresh choices before new selections instead of hard-coding the seed list.

schema.title: Response List Cities Api Cities Get

get.x-mobile-screen: Customer order creation /request; courier onboarding/profile editing
get.x-audience: Customer, courier, or signed-out visitor; no bearer token
get.x-before: None; load before showing city selector

post.description: Submit the user's Saudi mobile number when they request sign-in or resend a code. The backend accepts common local formats and normalizes them to E.164; the response deliberately looks the same whether the phone already has an account. Start the resend countdown from `expires_in`. Numeric five-digit `otp_dev` is returned only in development and omitted otherwise.
post.x-audience: Signed-out; no bearer token
post.x-before: None

post.description: Send the phone number and the five-digit development or six-digit non-development code entered on the OTP screen. If `is_new_user` is false, securely store the access and refresh tokens, use the returned role to choose the customer or courier experience, and fetch the profile. If true, carry the short-lived registration token to registration; never infer role from prototype phone fixtures.
post.x-audience: Signed-out; no bearer token
post.x-before: Successful send-otp and its five-digit development or six-digit non-development code

post.description: Create the account after OTP verification by sending the registration token and the chosen account role. Customer fields are optional at this API boundary; courier registration additionally requires city and at least one identity document in the service. Store the issued token pair only after success, then fetch `/me`. The current mobile prototype has no complete courier onboarding screen.
post.x-mobile-screen: Customer registration `/register-customer`; courier onboarding when built
post.x-audience: Signed-out with registration token; no bearer access token
post.x-before: `POST /api/auth/verify-otp` returning `is_new_user=true`
post.x-dependent-api: `GET /api/users/me`; courier verification review before courier operations

post.description: Rotate the current refresh credential when the access JWT expires or shortly before expiry. Replace both locally stored tokens atomically with the returned pair; a used token must never be retried in parallel because replay revokes its family. If refresh fails, clear local credentials and return to login. Do not send the refresh token as a normal bearer access token.
post.x-mobile-screen: Shared session restoration and background token renewal
post.x-audience: Holder of a refresh token; no bearer access token required
post.x-before: A previous login or registration token pair
post.x-dependent-api: Retry the originally requested protected API with the new access token

post.description: Call logout when the user explicitly signs out, then delete both stored tokens and close chat sockets. The backend revokes the account's access, refresh, and dashboard credentials across all devices before returning 204. Other devices must log in again. Even if the request fails, do not continue to show protected local data after the user chooses to sign out.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Valid access JWT
post.x-dependent-api: Clear local credentials; next use starts at `/login`

get.description: Fetch the authenticated user profile after restoring a session and whenever the profile screen opens. Use the generated seven-digit public_identifier as a display identifier, but keep the UUID id for API paths. Customers have no rating fields; courier rating and count are under courier_profile and are derived from customer reviews. Use server role and status for navigation instead of saved prototype fixtures.
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token

patch.description: Send only fields the user changed; omitted properties leave existing values untouched. The seven-digit public_identifier is generated and read-only, so do not submit it. Customer and courier users can edit common details, while courier city and biography apply to courier profiles. Use the returned profile as the new display state. Courier ratings are derived from reviews and cannot be edited through this route.
patch.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
patch.x-dependent-api: Refresh `GET /api/users/me` or update local profile from response

post.description: Use this action only after a courier has corrected a rejected profile and requests another verification review. It does not verify the courier immediately; the response returns the updated account and courier status for the UI. Do not expose it as a routine profile-save button. Operational courier endpoints remain unavailable until the profile is active and verified by the backend.
post.x-audience: Authenticated courier with rejected profile; bearer access token
post.x-before: `GET /api/users/me` shows rejected courier verification

get.description: Retrieve a minimal public-facing profile for a customer or courier who shares an order or conversation with the caller. Use its seven-digit public_identifier, display name, and initials in chat or order detail. Rating and courier details appear only for courier profiles. The backend enforces the relationship; arbitrary account browsing is unsupported. Never expect phone, email, identity documents, or full private profile fields.
get.x-audience: Authenticated order or conversation participant; bearer access token
get.x-before: Obtain the other party's ID from an owned order or inbox item

get.description: Load the signed-in user's own wallet snapshot, not a wallet ID chosen by the client. Display balance, held balance, and available funds as decimal-string SAR amounts; never parse them through floating-point arithmetic for financial decisions. Refresh after payment, approval, or withdrawal activity. A courier must be active and verified before this operational wallet route is available.
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or eligible verified courier; bearer access token

post.description: Start a wallet funding attempt with a positive decimal-string amount. In development the fake payment flow may settle locally and return a null payment URL; production currently returns `PAYMENTS_DISABLED` before any intent or balance change because Dhamen is not integrated. The mobile UI must not present this as a working production checkout or treat a browser return as settlement.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer or eligible verified courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: `GET /api/wallets/me` and a user-entered positive decimal amount
post.x-dependent-api: Return to wallet and transaction list after settlement

post.description: Request a courier withdrawal by sending a positive decimal-string amount and Saudi IBAN, plus a unique `Idempotency-Key` header. The backend encrypts the IBAN and returns only its last four characters and request status. Reuse the same key for a retry of one logical request, not for a new withdrawal. Customers cannot call this route.
post.x-audience: Authenticated active verified courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: `GET /api/wallets/me` confirms available funds
post.x-dependent-api: Refresh wallet and transactions; no courier withdrawal-list API exists

get.description: Read the owner's ledger entries newest first using `limit` and the returned `next_cursor`. Each item contains signed decimal-string amount, transaction type and status, balance after, and creation timestamp. Append pages without inventing totals from only the loaded slice. The backend provides no date-range filters or statement summary, so the courier statement screen cannot be fully integrated from this endpoint alone.
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or eligible verified courier; bearer access token
get.x-dependent-api: Same endpoint with `next_cursor` for more rows

post.description: Request a five-minute signed URL for one JPEG or PNG, declaring whether it is an order request photo or delivery proof. Upload bytes directly to the returned URL with the issued `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and `If-None-Match: *` headers; the API does not receive the file body. Keep the returned storage key for confirmation and later attachment to the matching operation.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Choose image, purpose, MIME type, and exact byte size

post.description: Confirm an uploaded object by its server-generated storage key after the direct PUT completes. The backend checks ownership, declared type and size, actual object presence, and image magic bytes. Only confirmed keys may be attached, and each can be claimed once for its original purpose. A local file URI or an unconfirmed key is not a durable order or delivery attachment.
post.x-audience: Authenticated owner of the upload grant; bearer access token
post.x-before: Successful direct PUT from `POST /api/media/upload-urls`

post.description: Create a gift request for a selected city and Gregorian delivery date. No delivery location URL is collected. Send up to three confirmed order-request media keys, not local file paths. The backend returns a new order UUID and computes financial totals later through invoice and settlement flows. Do not submit a client-calculated order total, commission, or courier payout.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer; bearer access token
post.x-before: Optional `POST /api/media/upload-urls` → direct PUT → confirm for 0–3 photos

get.description: List only orders owned by the customer or assigned to the courier, newest first. Use optional status filtering and cursor pagination to build current and history tabs; the server does not provide text search, order-number search, or a date-range filter. Courier availability is a separate route. Keep server status strings authoritative and derive display grouping locally without assuming the prototype's labels are API values.
get.x-mobile-screen: Customer/Courier Home `/home`; Orders `/orders`; Courier Calendar `/calendar` partial
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or eligible verified courier; bearer access token

get.description: Load a paginated radar of `NEW` orders in the courier's city. Summaries omit customer identity and full media; precise delivery locations are not collected. Use this list for selection rather than a full private detail screen. The courier cannot read an unassigned order's participant detail through the normal detail route. Accepting is an explicit action and may fail if another courier wins the race.
get.x-mobile-screen: Courier Orders `/orders` available tab; Home `/home` radar
get.x-audience: Authenticated active verified courier; bearer access token
get.x-before: Courier verification complete; matching city stored on profile

get.description: Fetch the authoritative state of an order the caller participates in. Customers can inspect their own order; couriers gain access once assigned. The response includes status, city, delivery date, computed total, assignment time, and an optional map URL. Hide map actions when that value is null. Fetch conversation identity by order ID, then use paginated REST messages for durable chat history.
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or assigned eligible courier; bearer access token
get.x-before: Order UUID from create, owned list, or accepted order
get.x-dependent-api: Active invoice, participant profile, chat, rating, or state transition

post.description: Claim a `NEW` order as the current verified courier. The backend checks city, assignment capacity, and current order state under locks; the first valid acceptance wins. Do not show assignment as complete until the response succeeds, because another courier may accept concurrently. The response provides the assigned order detail; use its UUID and status to open chat and later issue an invoice.
post.x-mobile-screen: Courier Orders `/orders` available tab; Order detail `/order/[id]`
post.x-audience: Authenticated active verified courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: `GET /api/orders/available` supplies a `NEW` order UUID

post.description: Cancel a participant order before work is in progress, optionally recording a short reason. The service rechecks the locked state, so a concurrent acceptance or payment transition may cause a rejection; display the server result rather than optimistic finality. A known backend gap can leave an issued invoice and wallet reservation pending when cancelling from `WAITING_PAYMENT`; do not promise immediate funds release in that state.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer or assigned eligible courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Participant order still in a cancellable pre-progress state

post.description: Submit one to five confirmed delivery-proof photo keys and an optional note after completing delivery. The backend checks courier assignment, order state, and ownership and purpose of each image before marking the order delivered. It does not collect precise delivery locations, calculate distance, or verify physical presence. This is a state transition, not a generic photo-upload call.
post.x-audience: Authenticated active verified assigned courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Order `IN_PROGRESS`; 1–5 confirmed `DELIVERY_PROOF` image keys

post.description: Approve the courier's delivered order when the customer accepts the proof. The backend completes the order and releases escrow according to its financial rules; the request has no body. Treat the returned status as authoritative, then refresh related wallet and rating state. A courier cannot approve on behalf of the customer. If the customer disagrees, use the dispute action instead of approval.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer who owns the order; bearer access token
post.x-before: Order is `DELIVERED` and proof reviewed

post.description: Open a dispute with a reason of at least three characters when a delivery or financial outcome is contested. The backend freezes the appropriate escrow path and returns a dispute ID and status. Show that resolution is pending; there is no customer/courier resolution endpoint. Do not infer a refund or payout from successful dispute creation, because an administrator must resolve it later.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer or assigned eligible courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Participant order in a disputable state
post.x-dependent-api: Refresh order; admin resolution occurs outside mobile API

post.description: Issue an itemized invoice for an assigned order. Send line titles, net unit prices, quantities, tax fractions, optional descriptions, courier fee, and optional promo code as decimal strings where applicable. The server computes service fees, discounts, tax, totals, revision-backed storage, and expiry. Use the returned invoice amounts; the mobile app must not send or calculate a trusted final total.
post.x-audience: Authenticated active verified assigned courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Accepted `ASSIGNED` order; collect 1–20 line items

get.description: Fetch the current active invoice for a participant order when the UI knows the order UUID but not the invoice UUID. Render the server's itemized amounts and status as decimal strings. This route is for the active invoice, not an invoice history list; a cancelled or expired invoice may no longer be the active result. Use the returned ID for payment or invoice-specific navigation.
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or assigned courier participant; bearer access token
get.x-before: Owned/assigned order with an active invoice
get.x-dependent-api: `GET /api/invoices/{invoice_id}`, promo preview, pay, or courier cancel

get.description: Read one invoice by its UUID after participant ownership checks. Unlike the order-scoped active-invoice route, this address can identify the particular invoice the screen is showing, including one whose status has changed. Display item lines, fee breakdown, promo snapshot, issue and expiry times, and total directly from the response. The backend does not expose saved card details or a collection of invoice revisions.
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or assigned courier participant; bearer access token
get.x-before: Invoice UUID from creation or active-order invoice
get.x-dependent-api: Customer payment or courier cancellation when eligible

post.description: Ask the backend to fund an issued invoice using its own wallet/gateway split rules; there is no client-selected amount or payment-method body. A `PENDING` response may contain a URL for gateway completion, while `PAID` indicates settlement in supported flows. Production currently returns `PAYMENTS_DISABLED` because live Dhamen is not implemented. Never treat a browser redirect alone as proof of payment.
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer who owns the invoice order; bearer access token
post.x-before: Issued invoice and, if using wallet funds, current wallet snapshot
post.x-dependent-api: Refresh invoice, order, wallet, and transactions after verified settlement

post.description: Let the issuing courier cancel an unpaid invoice to correct item lines or fees. The backend releases its promo and pending wallet reservation, marks the invoice cancelled, and reopens the order for a new invoice. It rejects already paid or otherwise ineligible invoices. Refresh the order and invoice display after success; do not edit the immutable original invoice in place.
post.x-audience: Authenticated issuing courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: Issued, unpaid invoice on assigned order

post.description: Preview a promo against the customer's own order and active invoice before showing a discounted total. Send the code and order UUID; the backend checks eligibility and computes the proposed discount. This endpoint does not reserve, consume, or settle the promo. Treat the response as a preview only, and continue to use the final invoice/payment response as the authoritative charged amount.
post.x-mobile-screen: Customer Invoice and checkout `/invoice/[id]` promo entry
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer who owns the order; bearer access token
post.x-before: Active invoice for `order_id`
post.x-dependent-api: Review discount; payment or courier invoice creation owns actual reservation

post.description: This callback is for the local simulated gateway, not a mobile app action and not a Dhamen endpoint. Its raw JSON body identifies a simulated payment link, status, and amount; the signature header authenticates the exact bytes. The backend handles idempotent settlement or failure in a transaction and returns an outcome. Never place the simulation signing secret in a phone app.
post.x-audience: No bearer token; valid `X-Webhook-Signature` over raw body; absent in production
post.x-before: A simulated payment intent in nonproduction and gateway test signature

post.description: After an order reaches COMPLETED, its customer may rate the assigned courier once with an integer score from one to five and an optional comment. The backend derives the rated courier from the order, so never submit a target user ID. Couriers cannot rate customers through this route. Use current_actor_has_rated to hide repeat submission and display a rating only after the request succeeds.
post.x-audience: Authenticated order customer after COMPLETED status; bearer access token
post.x-before: Order completed and caller has not already rated it

get.description: Fetch a courier aggregate rating and count computed from customer reviews of completed orders. The response includes a decimal-string average and integer count, not detailed review rows. The route requires authentication but does not require a shared order with the courier. Use the average only for display; never treat it as a stored field on the generic user record or a client-editable score.
get.x-audience: Any authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
get.x-before: User UUID from an order or participant profile
get.x-dependent-api: Optionally participant profile or rating action on completed order

get.description: List the caller's conversations ordered by recent activity. Each row provides its order and other-user IDs, last message preview, unread count, and timestamp; the response is cursor paginated. Use the returned `conversation_id` to open chat, not the order ID as a substitute. This API contains safe inbox data only for the participant and can support a home notification badge.
get.x-mobile-screen: Chat inbox; Customer/Courier Home `/home` optional summary
get.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
get.x-before: An accepted order creates a conversation
get.x-dependent-api: Messages page or WebSocket for selected conversation

get.description: Load decrypted conversation messages newest first in bounded pages. Pass next_cursor unchanged to the same route to retrieve older messages and stop when it is null. Membership is enforced; missing or foreign-conversation cursors return 404 instead of restarting history. Open the WebSocket for live updates, but fetch REST history after reconnect because socket events are not replayed. Deduplicate merged messages by id and acknowledge reads only when visible.
get.x-audience: Authenticated conversation participant; bearer access token
get.x-before: Conversation ID from inbox after order assignment
get.x-dependent-api: Same endpoint with next cursor; WebSocket or REST send

post.description: Send a text message with a nonempty `text` field, at most 4,000 characters. The server encrypts it at rest, commits it, publishes a live event, and sends a generic push notification without message text. Show the returned message after success and reconcile it with a matching WebSocket event to avoid duplicates. This route does not accept media attachments or arbitrary recipient IDs.
post.x-audience: Authenticated conversation participant; bearer access token
post.x-before: Conversation exists and actor is a participant
post.x-dependent-api: WebSocket receives committed event; refresh messages/inbox as needed

post.description: Acknowledge the caller's inbound messages as read and clear that conversation's unread count. The request has no JSON body and returns 204 without a payload. Call when the chat is genuinely visible to the user, rather than immediately on a background push event. Other participants' read state cannot be set by this caller. Refresh the inbox badge after success if necessary.
post.x-audience: Authenticated conversation participant; bearer access token
post.x-before: Conversation and visible messages loaded
post.x-dependent-api: Refresh inbox unread count if displayed

post.description: Register or refresh the current device's push token using `IOS` or `ANDROID`. The server associates that token with the authenticated account and can move a handed-down device token away from a previous owner. Register again after token rotation or a successful new login. Do not confuse this with an in-app notification-list API; the backend has no endpoint to fetch a notification feed.
post.x-mobile-screen: Shared app startup/login; notification permission flow
post.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
post.x-before: OS push token obtained after user permission
post.x-dependent-api: Push delivery for order and chat notices; delete on sign-out

delete.description: Unregister the current device's push token when push permission is removed, the token changes, or the user signs out. Send the exact token in the JSON body; the backend removes it only if owned by the caller. The response is 204 with no body. Logout revokes credentials, but the UI should also explicitly remove device registration when it still has a valid access token.
delete.x-audience: Authenticated customer or courier; bearer access token
delete.x-before: A token previously registered by this account

get.description: Use this endpoint only to confirm that development-only routes were registered on a local environment. It returns a static `dev` marker and is intentionally absent in production, where the same URL returns 404. It provides no user, order, payment, or service readiness data. Mobile integration should never depend on it; use the actual protected endpoints for screen data and operator readiness separately.

schema.title: Response Dev Ping Api Dev Ping Get

get.x-audience: No bearer token; development environment only

post.description: Trigger a correctly signed local fake callback for a pending simulated payment link. This development helper looks up the server-side amount, constructs the fake event, and runs the ordinary simulation webhook handler; it is not a real checkout or Dhamen integration. Never call it from a distributed mobile build or expose it as a customer payment button. Production does not register this route.
post.x-audience: No bearer token; development environment only
post.x-before: Simulated payment link ID from a local fake checkout
post.x-dependent-api: Server callback settlement; inspect normal invoice/wallet/order reads

get.description: When a customer or courier reopens any assigned order, including a completed order, use its order ID to find the conversation ID directly. This avoids scanning every page of the inbox for an old thread. A missing, unassigned, or unrelated order returns 404. Once found, request the first REST message page, then follow its cursor for older history. Open the WebSocket only when live updates are needed.
get.x-audience: Authenticated order customer or assigned courier; bearer access token

post.description: Save a special date; automatic reminders and annual recurrence are not available.
post.x-audience: Authenticated CUSTOMER; own records only
post.x-before: Customer login; saved occasion UUID for record operations
post.x-dependent-api: Reload occasion detail or list after changes

get.description: List owned dates, soonest first, with an optional inclusive date filter.
get.x-before: Customer login; saved occasion UUID for record operations
get.x-dependent-api: Reload occasion detail or list after changes

get.description: Read a saved date belonging to this customer.
get.x-before: Customer login; saved occasion UUID for record operations
get.x-dependent-api: Reload occasion detail or list after changes

patch.description: Update supplied fields on a customer-owned date.
patch.x-before: Customer login; saved occasion UUID for record operations
patch.x-dependent-api: Reload occasion detail or list after changes

delete.description: Delete a customer-owned date; return no response body.
delete.x-before: Customer login; saved occasion UUID for record operations
delete.x-dependent-api: Reload occasion detail or list after changes

x-websocket.description: Open this WebSocket only while the conversation screen needs live updates. Send JSON text frames shaped as `{"text":"..."}`; the server persists accepted messages before publishing message-shaped JSON events to participants. Invalid, oversized, or throttled frames may be dropped. Reconnect with a fresh access token after refresh, close on logout, and fetch REST history after reconnection because pub/sub is not a durable replay log.
x-websocket.authentication: Access JWT in token query parameter; conversation membership required
x-websocket.before: Conversation ID from inbox and a valid access token
x-websocket.dependentApi: Use REST messages/read for history and unread state
